title: The Drowned Oath Revisited
premise: Bram Vasquez, the youngest and least powerful member of the Ledgerkeepers—a guild that trades in impossible things—keeps their books and their secrets, preferring invisibility to the guild's dangerous bargains. When a dying courier presses a salt-stained map into Bram's hands, they learn it leads to the Hollow Crown, the ancient artifact binding a long-dead king's oath to the living monarch, and that the thing wearing the king's face has begun trading in winters that never end. Pursued by the guild's enforcers, Bram gathers an unlikely found family—a defected enforcer, a river-witch, and the king's exiled daughter—and discovers the map can only be read by someone willing to give up a memory they love. In the drowned vault beneath the capital, Bram must choose between unbinding the king and preserving their own forgotten past, ultimately sacrificing their memories of the guild to shatter the Crown and end the endless winter, then choosing to rebuild a new family from the people who stayed.
about_author: Rosalind Montrose is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging maritime trade records before turning to fiction, a past that seeps into her obsession with ledgers, oaths, and things lost to deep water. She writes fantasy about quiet people forced into loud destinies from a coastal cottage she shares with too many cats and one very opinionated heron.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In the Ledgerkeepers' fog-bound hall, Bram catalogs impossible trades—a bottled lullaby, a debt paid in shadows—while the guild's elders argue over rumors of a winter that won't lift. Bram's invisibility among the guild is established as both comfort and cage. Emotional beat: the ache of being essential yet unseen.

chapters.title: Salt on the Doorstep
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A courier collapses at the guild's back door, pressing a salt-stained map into Bram's hands and whispering 'the Crown remembers' before dying. Bram hides the map as enforcers arrive asking questions. Emotional beat: terror and the first pull of a larger story.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Omit
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Investigating the map, Bram finds pages razored from the guild's oldest ledger—records of a trade made with a king, centuries ago. Master Corvane, the guild's head, catches Bram searching and offers friendship with too-sharp edges. Emotional beat: the discovery that safety was always a lie.

chapters.title: The Enforcer Who Looked Away
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The guild's chief enforcer is ordered to retrieve the map and silence Bram, but Sefa—haunted by a purge she once enforced—warns Bram instead and defects. Together they flee the hall through the flooded undercity. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into loyalty; the first bond of found family.

chapters.title: A River-Witch's Price
chapters.summary: Ilyen's POV. The river-witch Ilyen reads the map's true nature: it shows the drowned vault beneath the capital, where the Hollow Crown binds the king. She joins them, but reveals the map's cost—only a willing sacrifice of a cherished memory can open the way. Emotional beat: dread of what each of them might lose.

chapters.title: The Daughter in the Frost
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In the frozen borderlands, the party finds Princess Averil, exiled for claiming her father 'isn't her father.' She confirms the thing wearing the crown has traded the kingdom's warmth for power. Bram and Averil clash over duty versus survival. Emotional beat: love against duty, sharpened into argument and reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The guild master, revealed as the Crown's oldest broker, offers Bram absolution and status in exchange for the map—and reveals Bram's own past was purchased by the guild long ago. Bram refuses. Emotional beat: the seduction of power and its corruption, refused at great cost.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The endless winter reaches its killing pitch; refugees choke the roads while the guild's enforcers hunt them. In a night battle on the frozen river, Ilyen is gravely wounded holding the passage open. The party reaches the capital's drowned gates. Emotional beat: grief and resolve fused; no turning back.

chapters.title: The Drowned Vault
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Beneath the capital, Bram faces the Hollow Crown and the hollowed king, with Averil and the dying king's last true self pleading for release. Bram pays the map's price—surrendering every memory of the guild—and speaks the unbinding. The Crown shatters; the true king dies free; the winter begins to break. Emotional beat: sacrifice, climax, and the terror of a self erased.

chapters.title: A Ledger Rewritten
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Spring thaws the capital. Memoryless but not unmoored, Bram finds the guild dissolved, Corvane gone to ground—and Sefa, Ilyen, and Averil waiting, carrying the stories Bram can no longer hold. Bram begins a new ledger, first entry: the names of the people who stayed. Emotional beat: quiet hope; found family as the true inheritance.
